newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus market shows signs of recovery.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus market shows signs of recovery.

text.p: Cyprus stocks rose 3.2 percent in the week ending Friday, reversing declines sparked by instalments on partly paid shares draining cash from the market.

The 41 share Cyprus Stock Exchange index, which is set at 100 points, closed at 84.48 on Friday, continuing the upward trend which started on October 4 when the market showed the first signs of recovery.
Last Friday the exchange closed at 81.87.
Many floor traders had attributed the drop to partly paid shares absorbing liquidity from the market.

"The uninterrupted upward momentum observed over the last five trading days suggests that the market will soon reach at least last year's levels," CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation said in its weekly stockmarket report.

"Most factors negatively impinging on investor sentiment, as for instance several large calls falling due on certain partly paid stocks have already been discounted to a large extent by the market," it said.

Significant gains were made in six of the seven sub-indices. The tourist enterprises sub-index remained stationary at 75.27 points, from 75.32 last week as official figures suggest tourism arrivals this year are down by up to four percent.
The banking sub-index closed at 91.61, gaining 3.4 percent from last week's closing figure of 88.60.

Fully paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed at 348.5, gaining nine cents from last week's close of 339.5. Fully paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank made gains of 12.5 cents in the week to close at 324.5.
Hellenic Bank fully paid shares closed at 256.5, gaining 17.5 cents from last week's close.
Insurance company stocks, which have taken a hammering since the official stock exchange opened on March 29, closed higher at 62.75 from 61.50 last week.
